full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed, J : These three Rules have been issued under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Criminal Misc. Cases 747/98, 2158/94 and 1191/94 on the prayer of the accused petitioners, namely, Mizan, Sadek and Shahidullah. Their common prayer is for quashing the impugned judgment and order dated 21.11.1993 passed by the Special Tribunal No. 3, Narayanganj in Special Tribunal Case on 56 of 1992 convicting each of them under section 376 of the Penal Code and sentencing each of them of suffer R.I. for seven years with a fine of Tk. 5,000/- each, in default, to suffer R.I. for six months more. 

 2. The informant Hafiza Begum, the victim who is said to be aged of 24/25 years and a married woman lodged the FIR on 15.9.89 in the local Rupgonj police station in the district of Narayanganj leading to G. R. 101/89 corresponding to Rupgonj P.S. Case No. 7 dated 15.9.89 under section 376 of the Penal Code. 

 3. The prosecution case is that the victim was married seven years back to her husband Abu Sayeed of Bhola co-village, P.S. Rupgonj, District. Narayanganj and by this time she gave birth to two daughters. Her husband is a day labourers on 13th May, 1989 at night after taking her night meal, she along with her husband and one daughter Rekha went to their bed and were asleep. At about 3/4 A.M., the accused Azmal, Sadek, Mizan and Shahidullah came to her residence and called out her husband to open the door on plea to have a glass of water. The victim then told them that at this dead of night, it was not possible to open the door and at this stage, the accused Mizan started scolding the husband of the victim and forcibly entered into her but by breaking upon the old door. A hurricane was then burning in the hut. The accused Mizan tried to put off the hurricane, but the victim resisted the same and they raised alarm being frightened that the accuses might commit some crime. Accused Mizan then dragged out the victim by catching her hair in front of the but of her sister-in-law (Nanad of the victim). Mizan was trying to violate the victim. She then tried to resist. Mizan raving failed to violate her chastity, started giving fists and blows upon the victim. The victim alleged that by the light of the said hurricane, she could clearly recognise accused Sadeque, Mizan, Azmal and Shahidullah to be present there. At the outcry of the victim and her husband, the husband of his sister-in-law Sanu Miah came out from his hut, but the accused Mizan then showed a dagger which he had been possessing in his hand and threatened the victim and also her brother-in-law and the sister-in-law and being frightened they closed their door. Then the accused Mizan forcibly took the victim to her own but and in front of her husband started raping her and the husband of the victim tried to raise alarm, but because of threatening, he could not. Mizan then dragged her forcibly. Then accuseds Azmal, Sadeque, Shahidullah entered into the but of the victim and started assaulting the husband of the victim. Then at first, the accused Mizan rapped her against her will in front of her husband and so also the accused Azmal who had a pistol in his hand. Shahidullah also followed by threatening the victim and then rapped the victim and lastly, accused Sadeque also did the same thing. All the four accused then went towards back of her hut, but Mizan came back again and left Tk. 200/- on the bed of the victim and threatened her that he left Tk. 200/- on the bed of the victim where the rape was committed and he would come again on the next night and she must return money and also threatened her not to disclose the occurrence to any body and saying this, they left the place of occurrence. 

 6. Police after investigation of the case, submitted the charge sheet being 97 of 1989 on 25.11.89 under sections 448/376 of the Penal Code and when the case was pending before the Magistrate, then out of four accused Sadeque and Mizan-appeared before the Magistrate and were,: released on bail. The accused Azmal absconding from the beginning. Shahidullah was arrested and he was in the custody. 

 7. From the different orders of the Magistrate such as 6.9.92, 10.10.92, 4.11.92, it appear that Sadek and Mizan although were granted bail, they later on, absconded and accused Azmal was all through absconding from the inception of the case and Shahidullah was produced before the Magistrate from the jail custody who was arrested by the police. 

 9. The case records were transmitted to the learned Sessions Judge as the case was triable under the Special Powers Act. The learned Judge, Narayanganj on 22.2.1992, as it appears passed the following order: 

 12. However, after opening the case for hearing, we felt that there is important question of law, with regard to the interpretation of section 27(6A) of the Special Powers Act which is of public importance. It is that after appearing before the court of Magistrate and being released on bail, if any accused absconds whether again the trial court as the Special Tribunal in this case shall have to comply with the provision of section 27(6) of the Special Powers Act. We then invited the learned Attorney General to address us on this law point. The learned Attorney General appeared before us and he made his lucid and clear submission on this point stating that under section 27(6A) of the Special Powers Act, if once an accused appear and is released on bail from any court, (including Magistrate Court or trial court) as provided in sub-section (6A) of section 27 of the Special Powers Act which is unqualified, the trial court is not under any legal obligation to comply with the provision of section 27(6) of the said Act. 

 13. The interpretation of sub-section (6) and (6A) of section 27 of the Special Powers Act is given by the learned Attorney General that, the words his release on bail as appearing in Sub-section (6A) is not qualified by any other word or words and it has been specifically said that released on bail by the trial Court or the Tribunal. The legislative intent according to the literal construction of sub-section 6(A) is very much clear as the first part of the sub-section 6(A) clearly says that in a case if any accused is produced or appearance of the accused person is made before the Tribunal and thereafter the accused person absconds or fails to appear in that case the procedure for trial in absentia as laid down under sub-section (6) shall not apply. The second part of sub-section (6A) clearly indicates that if any accused person to be tried by the tribunal is released on bail and then he absconds or fails to appear in that case, the procedure for trial in absentia as laid down under section (6) shall also not apply. 

 14. Here the power of releasing the accused person on bail is not confined to the tribunal only. The Magistrate during the investigation of the case can exercise the power of issuing the process warrant of arrest and granting bail as he exercise under the Code of Criminal Procedure in any other criminal case. Therefore even if the accused person is released on bail by the Magistrate who had no power to try the case sub-section 6(A) would be attracted and the procedure of sub-section 6 shall not apply. Consequently, the trial can be held in absentia which will not be without jurisdiction so as to enable the accused against whom the order of conviction has been passed by the tribunal in his absence to come under the purview of section 561 Cr. P.C. Section 27(6) of the Special Powers Act should be read with sub-section 6(A) of the. Section 27(6) of that Act which reads as follows : 

 "Where in a case after the production or appearance of an accused person before the Tribunal or his release on bail, the accused person absconds or fails to appear before it the procedure as laid down in sub-section (6) shall not apply and the Tribunal shall, after recording its decision so to do, try such person in his absence." 

 15. Ms. Salma Masud Choudhury, the learned Counsel for the petitioners argues, firstly, before us, relying on the judgment passed by a Special Division Bench in the case of Alamgir Hossain (Md.) Alias Alamgir Vs. The State, reported in 49 DLR, 630 that it is a case of no evidence, secondly, that for non-compliance of the mandatory provision of 27(6) by the Special Tribunal itself as trial court, the trial has been vitiated and therefore, the impugned judgment and order should be quashed. The second ground has not been taken In the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. However, she argues this as a point of law before us. 

 16. The Special Division Bench while deciding the aforesaid case, the question of jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure decided in the light of the Appellate Division's Decision as reported in 46 DLR (AD) 47 (Sher Ali (Md.) and other Vs The State), their Lordships of the said Special Division Bench in Para 26 of the said decision have held as under : 

 "Having given our anxious consideration to the materials on record and after hearing the learned Advocate of both the sides, we are of view that the dispute in question as raised in 46 DLR, 175 and 15 BLD 239 has been set at rest by the decision of our Appellate Division, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 67. A Convict may invoke the jurisdiction of this Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure if he can make case of common-Judice of the trial court or that the facts alledged do not constitute any criminal offence or the conviction has been based on no evidence or otherwise to secure the ends of justice and with that we add that he should approach the Court with clean hands." 

 18. The latest decision on the point of exercise of inherent jurisdiction under section 561A Cr, P.C. by the High Court Division has been formulated by the Appellate Division). in the decision of Sher Ali reported in 46 DLR. Here in this case, the prosecution examined as many as seven witnesses to establish the aforesaid allegations of rape committed by the accused upon the informant victim. The defence did not examine any witness, only Shahidullah faced trial and others absconded. Mizan and Sadek after taking bail from the court of the Magistrate absconded. They did not prefer any appeal against the impugned judgment and order of the trial court. Of late, they have come up with this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 19. For non-filing of the appeal, they gave given some lame excuse which are not acceptable at this stage. According to the decision, as provided in 16 DLR (AD) 67 as well as Special Division Bench since this court is not sitting as appellate court it cannot sift the evidence again or consider it as appellate court. So the argument of Ms. Salma Masud Chowdhury that it is a case of no evidence cannot be accepted at this stage without a grain of salt. Her second point that the trial court should have complied with provision of section 27(6) of the Special Powers Act also does not get any root to stand for our aforesaid discussions and the submission of the learned Attorney General because Mizan and Sadak appeared before the Magistrate and after getting bail they absconded Shahidullah faced the trial but he had not preferred by appeal under the statutory provision. So they cannot invoke the jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 20. The learned Counsel for the petitioners also could not convince us that according to the decision of the Special Division Bench the present impugned judgment and order suffers from Quram non-judice or on the facts and circum-stances of the case and the evidence on record, the offence is not constituted or that the petitioners have come up with clean hands. 

 23. It appears from the record that the accused petitioner Shahidullah who preferred Criminal Misc. Case No. 1191 of 1994 has been released on ad-interim bail on 7.8.1994 ad the accused petitioner Sadeuqe who preferred Criminal Misc. Case No. 2158 of 1994 has been released on bail on 17.12.1995 by the High Court Division. So their orders of bail are recalled and they are directed to surrender to their bail bonds immediately to the Deputy Commissioner, Narayanganj.
